knowledge_tree.title: Selective Compulsory English Book 2
knowledge_tree.content: High school English textbook focusing on themes like science, culture, food, travel, and first aid, with integrated skills development.

children.title: Unit 1: Science and Scientists
children.content: Explores scientific discoveries, the scientific method, and the lives of scientists.

children.title: John Snow and Cholera
children.content: Case study on how John Snow used data mapping to identify the source of a cholera outbreak.

children.title: The Scientific Method
children.content: Steps include asking questions, collecting data, analyzing results, and drawing conclusions.

children.title: Epidemiology
children.content: The study of how diseases spread and can be controlled.

children.title: Qian Xuesen
children.content: The father of China's aerospace program, highlighting his contributions and patriotism.

children.title: Stephen Hawking
children.content: His work on the big bang theory and his determination despite physical challenges.

children.title: Noun Clauses as Predicative
children.content: Grammar focus on clauses that follow linking verbs to rename or describe the subject.

children.title: Unit 2: Bridging Cultures
children.content: Discusses cultural exchange, studying abroad, and overcoming cultural shock.

children.title: Xie Lei's Experience
children.content: A Chinese student's adaptation to life and study in the UK.

children.title: Cultural Shock
children.content: The feelings of confusion and anxiety when exposed to a new culture.

children.title: Adaptation Strategies
children.content: Methods to overcome cultural shock, such as living with a host family and participating in social activities.

children.title: Debate on Studying Abroad
children.content: Arguments for and against studying abroad, considering economic, personal, and academic factors.

children.title: Chinese Language Learning Abroad
children.content: The role of Confucius Institutes in promoting Chinese language and culture.

children.title: Unit 3: Food and Culture
children.content: Examines the relationship between food and cultural identity.

children.title: Chinese Cuisine
children.content: The diversity and regional variations of Chinese food.

children.title: Sichuan Cuisine
children.content: Known for its bold, spicy flavors and use of peppercorns.

children.title: Shandong Cuisine
children.content: Features boiled dumplings and pancake rolls, emphasizing family meals.

children.title: Healthy Eating
children.content: Discusses the components of a balanced diet and the dangers of excessive sugar.

children.title: Past Perfect Tense
children.content: Grammar focus on actions completed before another past action.

children.title: Unit 4: Journey Across a Vast Land
children.content: Describes a train journey across Canada, highlighting geography and culture.

children.title: Canadian Geography
children.content: Features like the Canadian Rockies, prairies, and Great Lakes.

children.title: Cultural Insights
children.content: Experiences in cities like Toronto and Montreal, including multicultural aspects.

children.title: Discourse Markers
children.content: Linking words and phrases to show relationships between ideas.

children.title: Unit 5: First Aid
children.content: Provides knowledge and techniques for handling medical emergencies.

children.title: Types of Burns
children.content: Categorizes burns into first, second, and third degree based on skin damage.

children.title: First-Degree Burns
children.content: Affect only the top layer of skin, e.g., mild sunburn.

children.title: Second-Degree Burns
children.content: Damage layers beneath the top skin, causing blisters and more pain.

children.title: Third-Degree Burns
children.content: Destroy all skin layers and require immediate hospital care.

children.title: First Aid for Burns
children.content: Steps include cooling the burn, covering it, and seeking medical help if severe.

children.title: Heimlich Manoeuvre
children.content: Technique to help someone who is choking, developed by Dr. Henry Heimlich.

children.title: -ing Form as Adverbial
children.content: Grammar focus on using verb-ing phrases to indicate time, reason, or manner.
